adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unknown/misspelled usernames are silently skipped and the endpoint still returns success_json, so a mass add that added nobody looks identical to a full success

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. Any unknown/misspelled usernames are ignored with no tracking. After the loop it calls `group.save` and returns `success_json` if the save succeeds, even if zero users were actually added (e.g., all usernames invalid means no changes but `save` still succeeds). This makes “added nobody” indistinguishable from a full success at the API level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:77 — group.save` after `group.add` can only fail on the group record itself, so the `render_json_error` branch is effectively dead code and gives a false impression of failure handling

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code adds users via `group.add(user)` and then calls `group.save`, with a fallback to `render_json_error(group)` if `save` fails. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that `group.save` “can only fail on the group record itself” in a way that makes the error branch dead: we don’t see `Group#add`, validations, callbacks, or whether `group.add` mutates the group (e.g., counters) such that saving is required. Even if `save` is usually unnecessary after modifying associations, that’s more of an efficiency/style observation than a clear, provable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — No transaction around the add loop: an exception or validation failure partway through leaves an arbitrary prefix of users added while the client sees a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user, then only afterwards checks `if group.save ... else render_json_error`. There is no surrounding transaction and no rollback path. From the same diff’s prior implementation (`update_patch`) we can see `group.add(user)`/`group.remove(user)` were used without any final `save`, implying these methods likely persist membership changes immediately. If an exception occurs mid-loop, or if the final `group.save` fails, some members may already have been added while the request errors or returns a failure response, leaving a partially-applied change set (non-atomic update).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unbounded comma list with a per-username DB lookup and per-user side effects: one request can add tens of thousands of members (N+1 queries, no cap, no rate limit)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then `usernames.split(",").each` with `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop followed by `group.add(user)`. There is no cap/validation on the number of comma-separated usernames and no batching, so a single request with a very large list will trigger an N-per-username set of DB lookups and membership changes. That is directly verifiable from the added code and is an unbounded work/performance/DoS risk (even if the endpoint is admin-only).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — params.require(:usernames)` may return an Array (usernames[]=), and `.split` then raises NoMethodError → 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, if the client submits `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, `params[:usernames]` will be an Array, and Array does not respond to `split`, causing a NoMethodError (500). There is no type check/coercion in the diff, so the endpoint is not robust to a common parameter encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an Integer where AR expects records; depending on Rails version this raises or silently no-ops, and either way removing a non-member returns success

adjudication.rationale: In `remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an Integer from params. In Rails, `has_many`/`has_many :through` association `delete` commonly accepts either model instances *or ids* (it will resolve ids and delete the join row), so this is not verifiably an error from the diff alone. Also, the behavior “removing a non-member returns success” was explicitly tested/accepted in the prior code (the removed spec block included “succeeds silently when removing non-members”), so returning success on a no-op deletion is not clearly a regression/defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:92 — group.save` after the delete always succeeds, so remove_member can never report a real failure to the client

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the member removal is performed via `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which issues the delete on the association/join table immediately. The subsequent `group.save` does not validate or confirm that the association delete actually happened (and in the common case where the `Group` record itself is already valid and unchanged, `save` will simply succeed). As a result, the controller will almost always return `success_json` even if nothing was removed (e.g., user wasn’t a member) and it won’t catch real delete failures (which would raise and bypass the `if group.save` branch entirely). This makes the failure-reporting path effectively non-functional for the operation being attempted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally, so any PUT that omits `visible` silently flips the group to invisible

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the code sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. If a PUT/UPDATE request does not include the `visible` parameter, `params[:visible]` will be `nil`, the comparison returns `false`, and the group will be saved as invisible even though the caller did not intend to change visibility. This is directly verifiable from the diff: there is no guard like `if params.key?(:visible)` around the assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:37 — update has no automatic-group guard for alias_level/visible, so automatic/system groups can still be mutated despite the can_not_modify_automatic policy

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally allows updating `alias_level` and `visible` on automatic groups. In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, only renaming is blocked for automatic groups (`group.name = ... if ... && !group.automatic`), while `alias_level`/`visible` are always applied. This behavior is explicitly validated by the added spec: in `context ".update"` it updates automatic group `id: 1` with `visible: "true"` and asserts `group.visible.should == true` while name remains unchanged. So this is not a missed guard or policy violation introduced by the diff; it’s the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — total` and the paged query are two separate reads; concurrent add/remove makes pages skip or duplicate members and lets the UI show a stale total

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces two separate DB reads: `total = group.users.count` and then a second query for the page `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. Because they are not wrapped in a transaction/snapshot, concurrent membership changes can make `meta.total` inconsistent with the returned page (stale total). Additionally, with offset-based pagination, concurrent inserts/deletes in the ordered set can cause items to be skipped or duplicated across page requests. This behavior is a real consequence of the code as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit is attacker-controlled with no maximum, so `?limit=1000000` dumps the whole membership in one request

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly to the ActiveRecord query: `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no upper bound enforced. A request like `?limit=1000000` would cause the server to attempt to load/serialize up to that many group members (effectively the whole membership if smaller), which is a verifiable performance/data-exposure issue introduced by the change (previous code effectively constrained this behavior to automatic groups with a default/cap-like 200).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — Response shape changed from a bare array to {members, meta} and `get "users"` was dropped from routes, silently breaking existing API/plugin consumers with no spec covering this action

adjudication.rationale:
The diff makes two concrete, externally-visible interface changes:
1) In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, which will break any consumer expecting the previous array shape.
2) In `config/routes.rb` under the admin groups resource, the `get "users"` route is removed and replaced with `delete "members"` / `put "members"`, so any existing client hitting the old admin groups users endpoint will now 404.
While the core JS was updated to use the new `{members, meta}` shape, the change is still a silent API contract break for external/plugin consumers, and there is no spec added here covering `GroupsController#members` to assert/guard the new contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:94 — Automatic-group guard tests hardcode group_id/id 1 and rely on seed data being automatic; if seeding changes they pass or error for reasons unrelated to the guard

adjudication.rationale: The updated specs introduce multiple requests that hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` when asserting behavior for automatic groups (e.g. `.update` test: `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...`; `.add_members` test: `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...`). Nothing in the spec setup shown fabricates or guarantees a group with ID 1 exists and is `automatic: true`; it implicitly relies on seed/default groups having that ID and being automatic. That makes the tests brittle: changes to seed data/ID assignment could make them fail (missing record) or pass/fail for reasons unrelated to the automatic-group guard logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — remove_member rejection test uses PUT while the real route is DELETE, so the wrong request path is being verified
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out that the remove_member controller spec is making a PUT/XHR PUT request, but the actual route/action expects a DELETE request, meaning the test is using/verifying the wrong HTTP method/path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:103 — add_members spec only asserts the happy count; no spec covers unknown usernames, duplicate adds, array params, or partial failure, so the silent-skip behavior is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the new `.add_members` specs only cover (a) rejecting automatic groups and (b) adding two valid users, and do not exercise cases like unknown usernames, duplicates, or malformed input. However, that is a test coverage critique rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. The implementation intentionally silently skips unknown users (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), and the client code added (`Group#addMembers`) sends a comma-separated string, so “array params” is speculative and not evidenced as a required behavior in this diff. Therefore this finding does not identify a concrete bug/security/correctness problem in the changed code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:125 — No spec removes a non-member or a bogus user_id, so the always-success behavior of remove_member is green while wrong

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes membership editing to dedicated endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member`. In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, it does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, even if `user_id` was not a member or is bogus (no-op delete). However, the pre-existing behavior in the removed specs explicitly expected “succeeds silently when removing non-members”, so “always-success” is consistent with prior intent rather than a clear defect introduced here. The proposed finding is primarily about missing test coverage and speculates that the behavior is “wrong,” which is not verifiable from the diff as a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:12 — totalPages uses Math.floor(count/limit)+1 instead of ceil, so an exact multiple of limit yields a phantom empty last page and showingLast never fires on the real last page
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — offset is clamped to user_count, not to the last page start, so removing the last member of a page leaves the admin on a permanently blank page

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40 — removeMember/addMembers have no failure handler: a rejected request leaves the member list stale with no error shown, so the UI looks like the change applied

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `removeMember` and `addMembers` only update the UI by calling `findMembers()` inside the `.then(...)` success handler; they do not optimistically mutate `members` before the request completes. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20 — findMembers has no in-flight guard; overlapping add/remove reloads can resolve out of order and paint an older membership snapshot

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:24 — Add-members UI is only hidden for automatic groups client-side while update() still permits other mutations server-side; hiding is not a security boundary

adjudication.rationale: In group.hbs the “Add members” UI is hidden for automatic groups via `{{#unless automatic}}`, but the server-side endpoints that actually mutate membership (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member`) both explicitly block automatic groups with `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`. Also, `Admin::GroupsController#update` no longer accepts `usernames` and explicitly ignores name changes for automatic groups. While `update` still permits changing `visible`/`alias_level` for automatic groups, that’s a separate (apparently intended) capability and not a case of relying on client-side hiding for security.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:69 — Automatic-group check happens after Group.find but membership mutation endpoints have no per-user authorization beyond admin, so a CSRF/token-scoped admin action can rewrite any non-automatic group's membership wholesale with a single call

The finding claims there is “no per-user authorization beyond admin” and that this enables a CSRF/token-scoped admin action to rewrite membership wholesale. Nothing in the diff indicates missing admin authorization checks (they are implied by the controller inheritance), nor does the diff show CSRF protections being removed/disabled. Also, the endpoints do not “rewrite membership wholesale” in a single call: `add_members` only adds listed users, and `remove_member` removes a single `user_id` per request. Thus the finding is largely speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65 — New PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members endpoints take differently-shaped params (usernames CSV vs user_id) with no documented contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two new member-management endpoints with different required params: `add_members` requires `usernames` (CSV string) and `remove_member` requires `user_id` (integer) in `Admin::GroupsController`. However, this is an intentional and internally consistent API design in the diff: the client-side model calls match these shapes (`addMembers(usernames)` sends `data: { usernames: usernames }`, `removeMember(member)` sends `data: { user_id: member.get("id") }`). The proposed finding is about a lack of a “documented contract,” which is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect in the code shown, and nothing in the diff indicates runtime breakage due to the differing param shapes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — totalPages uses floor(user_count/limit)+1, yielding an extra empty page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same pagination bug: calculating totalPages as floor(user_count/limit)+1 creates an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, resulting in an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33 — next() clamps offset to user_count instead of the last page start, so the final "next" lands on an offset past the last page and shows an empty list
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the pagination bug where next() caps/clamps the offset to user_count/total rather than the last valid page start, causing the final 'next' to land at offset == total (past last page start) and display an empty list/page, creating confusing UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:41 — previous() subtracts limit from a clamped/misaligned offset, producing page offsets that are not multiples of limit and rows repeated across pages

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `next()` clamps `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, which can set `offset` to a value that is not a multiple of `limit` (e.g., `user_count=99`, `limit=50` => offset becomes 99). Then `previous()` computes `Math.max(offset - limit, 0)` (99-50=49), producing a non-page-aligned offset and causing overlapping/repeated rows across pages (page at offset 50 vs offset 49). The model’s `findMembers()` also only clamps to `[0, user_count]` and does not realign offsets, so the misalignment persists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:8 — currentPage divides by limit without guarding limit being 0/undefined, producing NaN/Infinity page numbers

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `limit` is defined on the `Discourse.Group` model with a default value of `50` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js` adds `limit: 50`). Since `admin-group.js.es6` is an `Em.ObjectController`, property lookups like `this.get("limit")` proxy to the model, so `limit` will not be `undefined` in normal operation. Also, both `currentPage` and `totalPages` guard the division when `user_count == 0` (the default for a new group), so the division only happens once members have been loaded and `limit` has a valid value (either default 50 or server-returned meta.limit, which defaults to 50 on the server). The diff does not introduce a concrete path where `limit` becomes 0/undefined, so the NaN/Infinity concern is speculative rather than a verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id) passes an Integer to a has_many collection that expects records, raising AssociationTypeMismatch / silently not removing the member

adjudication.rationale: In Rails/ActiveRecord, a `has_many` (including `has_many :through`) association collection’s `delete` method accepts either model instances or primary key ids. In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, `user_id` is coerced to an Integer and passed to `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which ActiveRecord will interpret as an id and remove the join row(s) without raising `AssociationTypeMismatch`. The diff doesn’t provide evidence that this association is a custom collection that rejects ids, so the claimed exception/silent failure is not a verifiable problem from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — params.require(:usernames).split(",") raises NoMethodError (500) if usernames arrives as an array rather than a string

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the request provides `usernames` as an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` or JSON array), `params.require(:usernames)` will return an Array, and `Array#split` does not exist, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. The diff contains no type normalization/guard to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — offset/limit are unvalidated: negative or huge values are passed straight to SQL LIMIT/OFFSET, causing errors or unbounded queries

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. This allows negative values (e.g., `limit=-1` or `offset=-1`) or extremely large limits to reach ActiveRecord and be translated into SQL `LIMIT/OFFSET`. Negative offsets can raise DB errors, and negative limits (notably on Postgres) can effectively remove the limit, leading to an unbounded query. The issue is directly present in the changed code path (now applies to all groups, not just automatic ones).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — total is counted separately from the paged query without a transaction, so meta.total can disagree with the returned page under concurrent membership changes

adjudication.rationale: In GroupsController#members, the code performs `total = group.users.count` and then issues a separate query `group.users.order(...).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. These are two independent SQL queries with no transaction or locking, so if group membership changes between them (users added/removed), `meta.total` can reflect a different state than the returned `members` page. This can lead to transient pagination inconsistencies (e.g., UI showing more/fewer total pages than the actual page data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers returns undefined for empty name instead of a resolved promise, so callers chaining .then() throw
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: some code paths in findMembers lack an explicit return, causing the function to return undefined (not a promise/value), which then breaks callers expecting a returned value (e.g., chaining .then()).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — offset is clamped to user_count (a stale client-side value, default 0) rather than the last page offset, silently resetting or overshooting pagination

adjudication.rationale: In group.js `findMembers` computes `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`, so an offset equal to `user_count` is considered valid. The admin controller’s `next` action can set exactly that value (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), `next` from offset 50 sets offset to 100, `findMembers` preserves 100, and the request will return an empty page. This matches the finding’s core claim (clamping to `user_count` instead of the last valid page offset causes overshoot). The “stale default 0” part is less central, but the overshoot bug is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:30 — result.meta/result.members are dereferenced without null checks, so an unexpected payload throws inside the promise with no error handling

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now calls `/groups/:name/members.json` and the corresponding Rails action (`GroupsController#members`) was changed to always return a JSON object with `members:` and `meta:` keys (`total/limit/offset`). Given this paired change, dereferencing `result.meta` and `result.members` is consistent with the server contract introduced here, so it’s not a verifiable defect in this diff. Also, if the payload were malformed, an exception thrown in the `.then` callback would reject the promise (it’s not “swallowed” inside the promise), so the “no error handling” part is generic robustness commentary rather than a concrete bug introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:45 — removeMember/addMembers fire findMembers without sequencing; rapid actions or overlapping page requests can resolve out of order and render a stale member list

app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:12 — setupController calls model.findMembers() without returning/awaiting it, dropping any rejection so member-load failures are silently swallowed

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AdminGroupRoute#setupController` was changed to call `model.findMembers();` and not return or chain the promise. In Ember, `setupController`’s return value is not used to control the transition, so any rejection from `findMembers()` will occur after the route has already set up/rendered and will not be handled via the route’s normal promise/error substates (unlike the previous `afterModel` which returned the `findMembers()` promise). This introduces a real correctness/UX regression: member-load failures won’t block the transition and won’t be handled in a structured way; they may surface only as an unhandled rejection/log rather than a route error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:9 — member loading moved out of afterModel and its promise is discarded, so errors no longer propagate to the route error handler

adjudication.rationale: In group-members.js.es6 the route previously returned the promise from `afterModel` (`return model.findMembers().then(...)`), which would allow a rejection to transition into the route’s error handling. The diff removes `afterModel` entirely and instead calls `model.findMembers();` inside `setupController` without returning/awaiting it. That discards the promise from the route lifecycle, so failures from the AJAX call in `findMembers` will no longer propagate through the route’s normal error substates/handlers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — update sets group.visible = (params[:visible] == "true"), forcing visible to false whenever the param is omitted from a partial update

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the line `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` executes unconditionally. If `params[:visible]` is omitted, `nil == "true"` evaluates to false, so `group.visible` will be set to false even when the request did not intend to change visibility. Unlike `alias_level`, there is no `if params[:visible].present?` guard, so the finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:74 — add_members ignores unknown usernames entirely and still returns success_json, so partial failures are not reported to the caller

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, unknown usernames are indeed skipped (`User.find_by_username` inside an `if`) and the action will still return `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. However, this is not a clear defect introduced by the diff: the previous incremental update path (`update_patch`) had the same behavior (silently ignoring non-existent users), and the removed specs explicitly asserted that behavior (“succeeds silently when adding non-existent users”). The diff does not establish that partial failures must be reported, so this reads as a behavioral preference/feature request rather than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:5 — Pagination math (currentPage/totalPages/offset clamping) lives in the admin controller while limit/offset/user_count state lives on Discourse.Group, splitting one concern across two layers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does place pagination-derived values (currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast) in the admin controller while the underlying pagination state (limit/offset/user_count) is stored on the Discourse.Group model (group.js). However, this is an architectural/concern-separation preference, not a clear defect (bug/security/correctness issue) that can be objectively verified as problematic from the diff alone. Nothing in the diff shows this split causing incorrect behavior by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:29 — next/previous actions duplicate the same "clamp offset, set, refetch" logic and reach into model internals instead of a single Group#loadPage helper

adjudication.rationale: The cited code does duplicate similar pagination logic in `next` and `previous` (compute clamped offset, set it on the model, call `findMembers()`), and it does access `model` properties directly. However, this is a refactoring/maintainability suggestion (DRY / encapsulation) rather than a verifiable defect, bug, security issue, or correctness problem introduced by the diff. The current implementation is consistent and functional as shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:14 — userCountDisplay computed appears unused now that admin template renders user_count directly

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not introduce a verifiable bug or defect here. `userCountDisplay` still exists on `Discourse.Group` and is only lightly reformatted (early return). While the admin template now displays `{{user_count}}` directly, that does not prove `userCountDisplay` is unused across the app; it may be referenced by other templates/routes not shown in the diff. Even if it were unused, that would be dead code/cleanup, not a correctness/security problem introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — Leftover "TODO: should clear the input" in addMembers ships an acknowledged incomplete behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `addMembers` action containing a comment `// TODO: should clear the input`. The comment only notes a potential UX improvement (clearing the input field) and leaving a TODO comment in code is not itself a concrete runtime problem evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:14 — Template mixes snake_case server field names (user_count) with camelCase computeds (currentPage), an inconsistent naming boundary

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `group.hbs`, `user_count` is a model attribute coming from the Rails/JSON API (the diff shows `Discourse.Group` uses `user_count` and the server returns `meta.total` etc.), while `currentPage`/`totalPages` are Ember computed properties defined on the controller. Using snake_case for persisted/serialized fields and camelCase for JS-side computeds is common in this codebase and does not create a functional defect. The finding points out naming inconsistency, but the diff does not show any breakage or incorrect binding caused by it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — User-supplied `limit` is unbounded, so `?limit=1000000` materializes and serializes the entire group membership.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)`. There is no upper bound or clamp on `limit`, so a request like `?limit=1000000` will cause the server to query and serialize up to that many users (potentially the entire group if it has fewer than that), creating a clear performance/DoS risk. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members runs one `User.find_by_username` query plus a `group.add` write per username with no cap on list size (N+1).

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop calls `User.find_by_username(username)`, which is one DB lookup per provided username (an N+1 pattern vs. a single `WHERE username IN (...)` query). There is also no validation/cap on how many usernames can be submitted, so a very large comma-separated list will trigger many queries and membership operations. The exact number of DB writes depends on what `group.add(user)` does internally, but the per-username query and unbounded loop are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Negative/huge offset and lack of max-limit clamping allow costly deep-offset scans on large groups.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to always use client-supplied `limit` and `offset`: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, and then applies `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound on `limit` and no clamping/validation of `offset`. This makes it verifiable that a request can ask for an arbitrarily large page size and/or a very large offset, which can cause expensive queries (large result sets and deep-offset scans) on large groups. Negative offsets are also not checked; behavior depends on ActiveRecord/DB, but the lack of validation is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:15 — Admin group index still loads and serializes all groups with no limit or pagination.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#index the code does `groups = Group.order(:name)` and then `render_serialized(groups, BasicGroupSerializer)` without any `limit`/pagination, so it will indeed return all matching groups. However, this behavior is not introduced by the diff (the index action already returned all groups before) and the finding is essentially a generic performance/pagination suggestion rather than a clear, verifiable bug/correctness defect caused by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:28 — Every add/remove member triggers a full findMembers refetch of the current page instead of a local update.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `removeMember` and `addMembers` both perform an AJAX request and then call `self.findMembers()` to reload members (and meta) from the server. However, this is not a verifiable correctness bug or clear defect introduced by the change—it’s an implementation choice to ensure the members list and `user_count/offset/limit` stay consistent with server state. The finding is essentially a performance/optimization suggestion (local mutation vs refetch), not a demonstrable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — findMembers() inside removeMember's then is unchained and uncaught, so a failed reload is an unhandled rejection leaving a stale member list.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, removeMember() returns the promise from the DELETE ajax call, but inside its `.then` it calls `self.findMembers();` without returning it. That means (1) callers cannot wait for the member-list reload to finish, and (2) if `findMembers()`'s ajax request rejects, that rejection is not chained to the returned promise (likely becoming an unhandled rejection / uncaught error), leaving the UI potentially showing stale members. The issue is directly visible in the diff: `}).then(function() { // reload member list self.findMembers(); });`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — addMembers' inner findMembers() is neither returned nor caught, producing an unhandled rejection and a member list that never reflects the addition.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, addMembers() returns the Discourse.ajax(...).then(...) promise, and inside the then-callback it calls self.findMembers() as a “fire-and-forget” refresh. That refresh will still run and, on success, will update model properties (including `members`) via setProperties in findMembers(), so the member list can reflect the addition. While the inner findMembers() promise is not chained/returned (so callers can’t await the refresh), the diff does not show any code relying on that return value, and the claim of an inevitable unhandled rejection and “never reflects the addition” is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers returns undefined when name is blank, so any caller doing .then() on it throws a TypeError.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now returns `undefined` when `name` is blank (`if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`). However, all visible callers that previously did `.then(...)` have been refactored to no longer chain promises (both `AdminGroupRoute.afterModel` and `group-members` route `afterModel` were removed; current calls are just `model.findMembers()` or return value unused). Within this diff there is no remaining verifiable `.then()` call on the result of `findMembers`, so the claimed immediate TypeError is not demonstrable from the changes shown; asserting that “any caller” will do `.then()` relies on code outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — addMembers action ignores the returned promise: an API failure (bad username, 422 automatic group) leaves the UI silent with the input still populated.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action does call `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without returning or chaining the resulting promise, so it is true that the promise is ignored. However, the proposed failure modes cited aren’t verifiable from the diff: (1) the UI only renders the add-members controls under `{{#unless automatic}}`, so a 422 for “automatic group” shouldn’t be reachable via this action as wired in the template; and (2) `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` silently ignores unknown usernames and still returns `success_json` if the group saves, so a “bad username” doesn’t obviously cause an API failure here. The claim that an API failure will leave the UI silent is therefore speculative/not supported by the diff (and the diff even suggests success is likely).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — removeMember discards the promise, so a failed DELETE gives the admin no error and the member appears removed pending reload.

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6 the `removeMember` action shows a `bootbox.confirm` and, on confirm, calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` but does not return or otherwise handle the AJAX promise from `Group.removeMember`. If the DELETE request fails/rejects, there is no `.catch`/error display path in this action, so the admin receives no feedback. However, the claim that the member "appears removed pending reload" isn’t directly supported by the diff because the UI list isn’t optimistically updated; `Group.removeMember` only reloads members on success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — setupController fires model.findMembers() fire-and-forget with no catch, so a failed member fetch is an unhandled rejection and the page renders an empty list.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Same fire-and-forget findMembers() with no error handling or loading state; previously afterModel blocked the transition and surfaced errors.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that findMembers() is now invoked asynchronously in a fire-and-forget manner without being awaited/handled (no blocking/loading/error handling), which can lead to the route/controller proceeding before member data is available (race condition).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:29 — next/previous mutate group.offset before the request; if findMembers rejects the offset stays advanced and pagination is permanently desynced from the shown members.

adjudication.rationale:
In admin-group.js.es6 the `next`/`previous` actions compute a new `offset`, immediately `group.set("offset", offset)`, and then call `group.findMembers()`.

`findMembers()` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and only updates `members` (and meta) inside the `.then(...)`. There is no error handling/rollback path. So if the request rejects, `offset` remains changed while `members` stays whatever it was before, making `currentPage`/`showingFirst`/`showingLast` reflect the new offset even though the displayed members are still from the previous page.

That inconsistency is directly introduced by the diff; whether it’s “permanent” depends on future successful reloads, but the desync-after-failure is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:11 — totalPages uses floor(count/limit)+1, so with an exact multiple showingLast never matches and next() pages past the end into an empty list.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. If user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 with limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. currentPage is Math.floor(offset/limit)+1, and next() advances offset via Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), so it can set offset to exactly user_count (100). Group.findMembers then requests /members.json with offset=user_count, which the server applies directly (limit/offset) and returns an empty members list. Because totalPages is too large, showingLast stays false on the real last page and allows paging into this empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members loops adding users then saves once with no transaction, so a mid-loop or save failure can leave the membership partially applied.
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — Unknown usernames are silently skipped and still return success_json, so the admin gets no feedback that members were not added.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each username is looked up with User.find_by_username(username); if no user is found, the code simply skips it (no error collected). After the loop it calls group.save and, if that succeeds (likely even when no members were added), it returns success_json. This means an admin can submit unknown usernames and still receive a success response with no indication that some/all adds were ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id) passes a raw id rather than a record and its result is unchecked, so a no-op or error still reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `has_many`/HABTM association `delete` explicitly accepts either records or raw ids, and it removes the join without deleting the user record. So “passes a raw id rather than a record” is not a verifiable defect. Also, the method then checks `group.save` and returns success on save; while it may report success even if the user wasn’t a member (a no-op), that behavior isn’t inherently incorrect and isn’t shown to be erroneous by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:54 — group.destroy return value is ignored; a callback-blocked destroy still renders success_json.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `destroy` action, the controller does call `group.destroy` and then unconditionally renders `success_json` without checking `destroyed?` or handling a false return. However, this exact behavior already existed in the pre-change code (the `destroy` method is effectively unchanged, just moved during refactor), and the claim about a “callback-blocked destroy” is speculative because no callbacks/constraints causing `destroy` to fail are shown in the diff. Thus it’s not a newly introduced or clearly verifiable defect based on this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit/offset are taken unbounded from params, so a huge limit forces an unpaginated serialization of the whole group.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupsController#members the code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to the query (`group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`) with no upper bound. A client can pass an extremely large `limit`, causing the server to load and serialize a very large number of users (potentially the entire group) in one request, which is a real performance/DoS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — None of the group membership ajax calls set a timeout, so a hung request leaves the admin UI waiting indefinitely with no feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new/updated group membership methods (findMembers/removeMember/addMembers) call `Discourse.ajax(...)` without an explicit `timeout` option. However, the diff does not show that a timeout is required, that requests are hanging, or that `Discourse.ajax` lacks a global/default timeout. This is a general robustness suggestion that would apply broadly across the codebase (and prior code also used `Discourse.ajax` without timeouts), not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — User-controlled `limit` param is now uncapped for all groups, allowing unbounded member dumps/DoS where the old code capped paging to automatic groups

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)`, with no enforced maximum. This means a client can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` to fetch/serialize a very large member list, potentially causing heavy DB/CPU/memory usage (DoS-style risk). The finding’s historical comparison is somewhat off (the old code also didn’t strictly cap `limit` for automatic groups, and non-automatic groups previously returned all members), but the core issue—an uncapped user-controlled `limit` being applied—is real and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — remove_member calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` directly instead of `Group#remove`, bypassing the model's membership-removal bookkeeping (user_count/notifications)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove_member` now does `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of the previously-used `group.remove(user)` approach (seen in the removed `update_patch`). However, the finding’s core claim—"bypassing the model's membership-removal bookkeeping (user_count/notifications)"—is not verifiable from the diff: there is no shown `Group#remove` implementation or any demonstrated callbacks/counter-cache/notification side effects that `group.users.delete` would skip. From what’s visible, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is a standard Rails way to remove an association and will persist the join-row deletion; it’s not clearly a defect in the shown code by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:66 — params.require(:group_id).to_i` coerces non-numeric ids to 0, turning bad input into an unhandled RecordNotFound/500 rather than a clean 404

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` in `add_members`/`remove_member`, and `to_i` will indeed coerce non-numeric strings to 0. However, the proposed impact (“unhandled … /500 rather than a clean 404”) is not verifiable from the diff: in typical Rails apps (and likely in Discourse), `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` is rescued and turned into a 404. Also, this pattern (`params[:id].to_i` then `Group.find`) already exists elsewhere in the same controller (`update`, `destroy`), so it’s not clearly a newly introduced defect in this diff. The claim about 500 is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:32 — visible` is still assignable on automatic groups even though rename/membership are blocked, an inconsistent restriction on system-managed groups

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is applied even for automatic groups, but the diff (and new spec) explicitly expects this behavior: the added test "ignore name change on automatic group" asserts `group.visible.should == true` after updating an automatic group. Also, the pre-diff implementation (`update_put`) already allowed changing `visible` on automatic groups (it only blocked rename/membership changes). So this is not a newly introduced defect, and it appears to be intentional rather than an inconsistent restriction bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members accepts an unbounded comma-separated username list with no size limit, enabling expensive bulk writes in one request

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` does split an arbitrary `usernames` string and iterates over all entries with no explicit cap. However this endpoint is under `Admin::GroupsController` (admin-only context) and the pre-existing code paths it replaces (`update_patch` with `changes[:add]` and `create/update_put` with `group.usernames`) likewise accepted arbitrary-length username lists without enforcing a size limit. So while a limit could be a nice hardening/perf improvement, the finding frames it as a concrete defect/security issue introduced by this diff; that is not clearly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20 — members pagination/meta rewrite (limit default 200->50, always-paginated, new JSON envelope) ships with no spec anywhere

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change GroupsController#members behavior (default limit 200→50, always paginated, and returns a new JSON envelope with {members, meta}). However, the proposed finding’s core claim—“ships with no spec anywhere”—is not verifiable from the diff alone. The diff shows changes/additions to Admin::GroupsController specs, but it does not prove that there are no existing specs for GroupsController#members elsewhere in the codebase. Lack-of-tests is also not, by itself, a clear correctness/security defect introduced by the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91 — no coverage for add_members with nonexistent username, empty/duplicate usernames, or already-member (silently-ignored paths deleted with the old incremental specs)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove prior incremental membership-change specs that covered edge cases (e.g., adding non-existent users, removing non-members), and the new specs for `add_members` only cover adding valid users and the automatic-group restriction. However, this is a test-coverage gap, not a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the code itself. The diff does not demonstrate incorrect behavior for these cases—only that they are no longer explicitly tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:112 — no coverage for remove_member with a user_id that is not a member or does not exist

adjudication.rationale:
The diff does introduce a new `remove_member` endpoint (`Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`) and adds a new spec context for it, but the proposed finding is about *missing test coverage* for edge cases (user_id not a member / does not exist), not about a concrete bug or correctness defect in the implemented code.

From the diff, it’s true those specific scenarios are not covered by any shown tests; however, lack of coverage is not itself a verifiable problem in the code’s behavior. Also, the implementation uses `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which in Rails typically no-ops for non-members/non-existent IDs, so there’s no clear indication this is incorrect.

Notably, the spec file in the diff is actually truncated at the end (`user_id:` with no value), which would be a real defect, but that is *not what the proposed finding claims*.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:83 — group.users.delete(user_id) passes an Integer to an association delete; the only spec would still pass on a no-op-vs-delete mismatch in other AR versions and no spec asserts the membership row itself is gone

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `group.users` is an ActiveRecord association collection. In Rails/AR, `collection.delete` is designed to remove records from the association (typically deleting join rows for HABTM/has_many :through) and commonly accepts either model instances or primary keys. Nothing in the diff establishes that this call is invalid or becomes a no-op, and the concern about “other AR versions” is speculative and not verifiable from the change itself. While it’s true the shown specs don’t explicitly assert the join row removal, that doesn’t make the implementation itself a clear defect based on the diff alone.
